questions.question: What should the FNP verify at the start of a telehealth visit?
choices: Only the patient’s email address
Identity, current location, call-back number, privacy/safety, and emergency plan
Only the insurance plan
Only whether the camera works
questions.explanation: Location and a call-back method are essential if the patient deteriorates or the connection fails. Privacy and emergency planning are part of safe virtual care.

questions.question: Which presentation is least appropriate for a prolonged routine telehealth assessment?
choices: Stable medication follow-up
Discussion of routine laboratory results
New severe chest pain with dyspnea and diaphoresis
Preventive counseling
questions.explanation: Potential emergency symptoms require immediate triage and an emergency pathway, not a prolonged virtual assessment.

questions.question: What is the best documentation practice for a virtual physical examination?
choices: Document a complete normal examination by default
Document observed findings, patient-reported findings, limitations, and unassessed elements
Avoid documenting the examination
Copy an in-person template
questions.explanation: Telehealth documentation must accurately distinguish what was observed from what was reported and what could not be assessed.

questions.question: A patient submits an unexpected very high home blood-pressure value. What is the best first clinical approach if the patient is stable?
choices: Automatically double medication
Ignore it because home devices are never useful
Assess symptoms and verify device, technique, timing, repeated measurements, and trend
Diagnose hypertensive emergency from the number alone
questions.explanation: Patient-generated data require context. Confirm technique and trend while assessing symptoms and deciding whether urgent evaluation is needed.

questions.question: Why is a remote-monitoring program unsafe without a named review process?
choices: Patients do not need to know their values
Data can be collected without anyone owning review, follow-up, or escalation
Monitoring devices cannot measure symptoms
It prevents teach-back
questions.explanation: Remote monitoring requires clear ownership, review expectations, escalation thresholds, and patient instructions. Data collection alone does not create safety.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a patient has no private space for a sensitive telehealth discussion?
choices: Proceed with detailed questions while others are present
Ask the patient to speak louder
Arrange a safer/private communication pathway and do not force disclosure
End all care permanently
questions.explanation: Privacy may affect safety and candor. Use an accessible alternative rather than forcing sensitive discussion in an unsafe setting.

questions.question: Which statement about virtual rash assessment is most accurate?
choices: A photo can always replace in-person examination
Video can show some features but cannot reliably assess all characteristics or systemic illness
A rash never needs urgent assessment
Parents can always determine blanching accurately
questions.explanation: Lighting, image quality, and the absence of palpation/systemic assessment limit virtual rash evaluation. Concerning symptoms or uncertain findings require escalation.

questions.question: What question helps determine if telehealth can answer a clinical problem safely?
choices: “Does the patient prefer video?” only
“What finding would I need to see, feel, hear, measure, or test to make this decision safely?”
“Can the visit be shorter?”
“Is there a portal account?”
questions.explanation: This question exposes whether the clinical decision requires an in-person examination, verified vital signs, laboratory testing, imaging, or emergency resources.

questions.question: A patient with worsening dyspnea has poor video quality and cannot obtain oxygen saturation. What is the safest reasoning?
choices: Wait for a better connection regardless of symptoms
Use the trajectory and limited assessment to lower the threshold for in-person or emergency evaluation
Assume normal oxygenation because the patient can speak
Treat the video problem as nonadherence
questions.explanation: Uncertainty plus worsening symptoms can make virtual management unsafe. Escalate according to clinical risk rather than waiting for technology to improve.

questions.question: Which action best promotes telehealth equity?
choices: Require video for every patient
Offer clinically safe alternatives, interpreter/accommodation support, and plain-language instructions
Assume older adults cannot use telehealth
Use portal messages as the only follow-up option
questions.explanation: Telehealth access varies. Safe care offers accessible options and supports rather than allowing technology or language barriers to create diagnostic delay.
